original_question: Do cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome and Carpenter syndrome share the same inheritance pattern?

final_qi.question: What is the inheritance pattern of cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome—best known as Greig cephalopolysyndactyly—is caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the GLI3 gene. Because only one altered copy of GLI3 is sufficient to produce the phenotype, the disorder is transmitted in an autosomal dominant pattern, giving affected individuals a 50 % chance of passing the syndrome to each child.

final_qi.question: What is the inheritance pattern of Carpenter syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Carpenter syndrome (acrocephalopolysyndactyly type II) is caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in genes such as RAB23 or MEGF8. Because disease manifests only when both alleles are affected and parents are typically asymptomatic carriers, the disorder follows an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance.
